title.en: Ionic bonding, extraction of metals and corrosion

text.en: Salt crystals are hard, and aluminium foil is made from a rock called bauxite. How are ionic compounds formed, and how are metals pulled out of their ores?

An atom of a metal loses electrons to form a positive ion and a non-metal gains electrons to form a negative ion. The attraction is an ionic bond.
Sodium chloride forms when Na loses one electron and Cl gains it, giving Na+ and Cl-. Both then have a stable octet.
Ionic compounds are hard solids with high melting and boiling points, are soluble in water and conduct electricity only when molten or dissolved.
A mineral is a natural substance containing a metal. An ore is a mineral from which the metal can be extracted profitably.
Metals low in the series (Hg, Cu) are got by heating the ore. Cinnabar HgS heated in air gives mercury.
Metals in the middle (Zn, Fe, Pb) are obtained from oxides by reduction with carbon. For example ZnO + C gives Zn + CO.
Metals at the top (Na, Ca, Al) are extracted by electrolysis of molten compounds, for example aluminium from molten alumina.
Rusting needs both oxygen and moisture. Prevent by painting, oiling, galvanisation (zinc coating) and alloying. Alloys like brass and bronze are mixtures of metals.

problem.en: How is zinc obtained from zinc blende?

text.en: Zinc blende ZnS is first roasted: 2ZnS + 3O2 -> 2ZnO + 2SO2.
The oxide is reduced with carbon: ZnO + C -> Zn + CO.

why.en: Zinc is in the middle of the series.

prompt.en: How does extraction depend on reactivity?

points.en: Ionic bond: transfer of electrons between metal and non-metal.
Extraction method depends on position in the reactivity series.
Rusting needs oxygen and water; prevent by galvanisation, painting, alloying.
